item.title: Void Linux: LUKS2 + Btrfs Guide
item.description:
A complete guide for installing Void Linux with LUKS2 full-disk encryption and a Btrfs subvolume layout that is compatible with snapshot tools such as Timeshift.

1. Disk Identification & Partitioning

Identify the target block device:

lsblk

Partition the disk with fdisk (or cfdisk for a TUI):

fdisk /dev/sdX

Partition Scheme (UEFI)

Create a GPT partition table:

  • g — create a new GPT partition table.
  • n — create partition 1, the EFI system partition (ESP). Accept the default first sector and use +200M (128M–1G is sufficient).
    • Wipe the signature if prompted: Y.
    • Set the type with t -> 1 (EFI System).
  • n — create partition 2, the boot partition. Accept the default first sector and use +2G (1G minimum, 2G recommended).
    • Wipe the signature if prompted: Y.
    • Set the type with t -> 20 (Linux filesystem).
  • n — create partition 3, the root partition. Accept the default first and last sectors to use the remaining space.
    • Set the type with t -> 20 (Linux filesystem).
  • w — write the changes and exit.

Note: This guide targets UEFI. On BIOS/MBR, skip the ESP, create a boot partition instead, encrypt /dev/sdX2, and install the grub package with grub-install /dev/sdX.

item.title: runit: Simple, Fast, Easy
item.description:
Overview

runit is a small init system built on one idea:

A service is a directory with an executable run script.

No unit files, no dependency graph, no enable database. If the directory exists and has no down file, runit runs ./run.

Root: system commands assume a root shell. Prefix with sudo or doas if needed. User services: run as yourself.

Editors: vi file, vim file, or nano file. In nano, use Ctrl+O, Enter, Ctrl+X to save and quit. In vi/vim, press i, type, then Esc, :wq, Enter.

item.title: Void Linux: LUKS1 + Btrfs Guide
item.description:
A complete guide for installing Void Linux with LUKS1 full-disk encryption, a Btrfs subvolume layout (Timeshift-compatible), and single-passphrase GRUB unlocking.

1. Disk Identification & Partitioning

Identify target block devices:

lsblk

Partition the target disk using fdisk (or cfdisk for a TUI interface):

fdisk /dev/sdX

Partition Scheme (UEFI vs. BIOS)

UEFI System (GPT Scheme)

  • Create GPT Partition Table: Command g
  • Create EFI System Partition (ESP) (128M - 1G recommended):
    • Command n -> Partition 1 -> First sector: Default -> Last sector: +200M
    • Wipe signature if prompted: Y
    • Change partition type: Command t -> Type 1 (EFI System)
  • Create Root Partition:
    • Command n -> Partition 2 -> First sector: Default -> Last sector: Default (Use remaining space)
  • Write Changes: Command w

BIOS / Legacy System (MBR Scheme)

  • Create MBR Partition Table: Command o
  • Create Root Partition:
    • Command n -> Primary -> Partition 1 -> First sector: Default -> Last sector: Default (Use entire disk)
    • Set bootable flag: Command a -> Partition 1
  • Write Changes: Command w

2. Encryption & File System Creation

Encrypt the root partition using LUKS1.
